script.title: Debt snowball vs avalanche: the math with three real-looking debts
script.hook: Smallest debt first, or highest rate first?

scenes.heading: Which debt first?
scenes.narration: You have three debts and some extra money each month. Do you kill the smallest debt first, or the one with the highest rate? Let's run both.
scenes.visual_brief:
#pergunta Smallest debt first, or highest rate first?
Open the loop.

scenes.heading: Two methods
scenes.narration: The snowball pays the smallest balance first. The avalanche pays the highest interest rate first. Both pay the minimum on everything else.
scenes.visual_brief:
#comparacao Snowball: smallest balance first; quick wins | Avalanche: highest rate first; less interest
Define both.

scenes.heading: Three debts
scenes.narration: Our example: a $1,500 store card at 18%, a $6,000 credit card at 26%, and an $8,000 car loan at 7%. These are made up numbers, just for the math.
scenes.visual_brief:
#lista Store card: $1,500 at 18%; Credit card: $6,000 at 26%; Car loan: $8,000 at 7%
The debts.

scenes.heading: The budget
scenes.narration: The minimums add up to $390. You can pay $690 a month, so $300 extra goes to one target at a time.
scenes.visual_brief:
#numero 300 | extra dollars a month toward one debt
The lever.

scenes.heading: Snowball run
scenes.narration: With the snowball, the store card is gone in month 5. That first win comes fast.
scenes.visual_brief:
#numero 5 | months to the first paid off debt with the snowball
Quick win.

scenes.heading: Avalanche run
scenes.narration: With the avalanche, the 26% card goes first. Your first payoff only comes in month 16.
scenes.visual_brief:
#numero 16 | months to the first paid off debt with the avalanche
Slower start.

scenes.heading: The finish line
scenes.narration: Snowball: all debt gone in 27 months. Avalanche: 26 months.
scenes.visual_brief:
#grafico Months to be debt free | Snowball=27; Avalanche=26
Almost the same.

scenes.heading: The interest
scenes.narration: Snowball costs $2,513 in interest. Avalanche costs $2,350. The avalanche saves $163.
scenes.visual_brief:
#grafico Total interest, in dollars | Snowball=2513; Avalanche=2350
The math winner.

scenes.heading: Why avalanche wins
scenes.narration: Paying the highest rate first shrinks the most expensive balance first, so less interest piles up every month.
scenes.visual_brief:
#causa Highest rate paid first => The most expensive balance shrinks => Less interest each month
The logic.

scenes.heading: So which one?
scenes.narration: Mathematically, the avalanche wins. But the snowball gives you a win in month 5 instead of month 16. The best method is the one you will actually stick to. This is math, not financial advice.

sources.title: Snowball vs. Avalanche for Paying Down Debt

claims.text: Snowball pays the smallest balance first; avalanche pays the highest interest rate first; both keep minimums on every debt.

Example debts: store card $1,500 at 18% ($40 minimum), credit card $6,000 at 26% ($150), car loan $8,000 at 7% ($200), with $690 a month in total. Snowball: first debt gone in month 5, all gone in 27 months, $2,513 interest. Avalanche: first debt gone in month 16, all gone in 26 months, $2,350 interest. Simulacao mensal propria.
